# Pzync

> Pzync is a free, open-source app that connects an Android phone to an Ubuntu (Debian-based Linux) or Windows computer over the local network. It sends files, syncs the clipboard, streams PC audio to the phone, and uses the phone as a wireless webcam and microphone. No account and no cloud server is involved in transfers.

## Key facts
- Platforms: Android 7.0+, Ubuntu / Debian-based Linux (amd64, .deb), Windows 10+ (x64, .exe)
- License: MIT
- Connection: direct over local Wi-Fi (UDP 8200 for discovery, TCP 8080 for data), encrypted with TLS, paired by confirming a matching code on both screens
- Android app collects anonymous usage analytics (Google Firebase); the desktop app has no telemetry

## Guides
- [Connect Android to Ubuntu](/connect-android-to-ubuntu): install the .deb, pair, firewall and webcam packages
- [Connect Android to Windows](/connect-android-to-windows): install, pair, firewall
- [Use an Android phone as a webcam](/android-phone-as-webcam): Ubuntu and Windows virtual camera setup
- [Transfer files between Android and a PC](/transfer-files-android-to-pc): Wi-Fi transfer with SHA-256 verification
- [Sync the clipboard between Android and a PC](/sync-clipboard-android-to-pc): text, screenshots, Quick Settings tile
